content.text:
I've checked the brief line by line against the release. Here are my findings.

**Key facts:** 8 of 10 stated correctly. Two are absent: ROTCE (29% / 23% ex-significant items) and net interest income ($25.6 billion, up 10%) — neither appears anywhere in the brief, which is a notable omission given ROTCE is the headline profitability metric in the release.

**Claims:** one clear error. The brief states a "reported overhead ratio of 4" where the release says 48% (the managed 47% is correct). Everything else — segment revenues, capital ratios, distributions, significant items, credit metrics — ties to the release.

facts.evidence: Reported revenue was $57.3 billion, with managed revenue of $58.0 billion.
Reported net income for the second quarter of 2026 was $21.2 billion ($7.70 per share)
net income excluding significant items was $16.9 billion ($6.14 per share)
Markets revenue was $12.1 billion, up 35%, driven by Equity Markets revenue of $6.0 billion, up 86%.
Monitor the impact of the $4.6 billion net gain related to Visa shares and $1.0 billion of gains on certain equity investments on future earnings volatility.
The firm executed common stock net repurchases of $6.2 billion and a common dividend of $4.0 billion ($1.50 per share).
The firm reported a Basel III common equity Tier 1 capital ratio of 14.1% (Standardized) and 14.2% (Advanced).
Credit costs were $2.5 billion, consisting of $2.4 billion of net charge-offs and a $149 million net reserve build.

Average deposits were up 7% YoY and 3% QoQ.

CCB Card Services & Auto net revenue was $7.8 billion, up 12%.
The increase in Card Services & Auto net revenue was driven by higher Card Services net interest income and higher auto operating lease income.
CIB net revenue was $24.9 billion, up 27%.

The release provides no guidance or outlook.

Total Loss-Absorbing Capacity was $590 billion.
The firm executed common stock net repurchases of $6.2 billion.
The firm paid a common dividend of $4.0 billion, or $1.50 per share.
Significant items included a $4.6 billion net gain related to Visa shares.
Significant items included $1.0 billion of gains on certain equity investments.
CCB net charge-offs were $2.2 billion, predominantly driven by Card Services.
Management cited risks including geopolitical tensions, wars, sticky inflation, large global fiscal deficits, and elevated asset prices.
